title: Deleting a gym leaves its payment company keys and payment records on our web server
what: When HQ deletes a gym, only the gym server and its files are cleared. Our separate small web database still keeps that gym's sealed payment company keys or sign-in tokens, every payment link record with member ids and amounts, and its AI limits. The keys are only wiped after a desk presses Disconnect, which a leaving gym may never do. Nothing removes the payment records at all.
expected: Deleting a gym also clears everything about it in the small web database, within the 30 days the data agreement promises, and the delete step says so.
fix_line: Make the gym delete also clear that gym's rows in the small web database, and log it

title: Nobody can tell from the code which changes to the small web database are live
what: The first line of several change files for the small web database still says not applied, although the features that need them are live: Verify with WhatsApp, AI help answers and the AI usage counts. Some files were applied one by one, so the database's own list of applied changes is not complete either. Running the standard apply step those files suggest could try to add a column that already exists and stop half way.
expected: Each change file says truthfully whether it is live, and one written list matches the database, so the next change is applied safely.
fix_line: Check the live list once, fix each file's first line, and write the apply rule in one place

title: The nightly clean-up, the 10-minute payment check and the help AI's monthly limit fail with only a hidden log line
what: If the nightly clean-up of crash reports, sign-in codes and friend form counts fails, or the payment check that marks links paid fails, the server only writes a log line nobody is sent. When the help box reaches its monthly AI spending limit, every person quietly gets no answer for the rest of the month, again with only a log line.
expected: Each of these shows up in HQ or the outage alarm: last good run time, failures, and when the monthly AI limit is reached.
how_often: whenever a job or key fails
fix_line: Write each job's last good run where HQ already reads, and warn on a miss

title: The small web database is left out of the written backup plan
what: The backup note covers only the gym server. The small web database holds demo requests, every help question and team reply, payment links and each gym's sealed payment keys. Nothing written says how it is backed up or how to bring it back after a bad change or a lost account. Cloudflare keeps its own restore points, but no note says so, for how long, or how to use them.
expected: The backup note lists this database too, with how long restore points last and the steps to restore it.
fix_line: Add the small web database to the backup note, with its restore steps

title: No written list of the about 17 secret keys this server needs, what each breaks, or how to replace one
what: This server uses about 17 secret keys: the help AI key, three other AI keys, the WhatsApp token and app secret, the sign-in code secret, the payment master key, six payment partner keys and a salt. Each is named only inside the code. The sign-in code secret must match a copy kept in the gym server, and nothing says how to change both together. No note says who holds each key, when it runs out, or what stops if it goes.
expected: One short note lists every key: what uses it, what breaks without it, when it expires and how to replace it safely.
how_often: when a key is lost or expires
fix_line: Write one key list for this server with replace steps
